parsed.explanation: The combined regime imposes a tier-1 universal exposure: restroom use is unavoidable, and in this division it is a crime (up to one year, first offence) in government buildings and public-facing private businesses including hospitals — the only such law reaching private premises, effective 1 July 2026. Discovery is engineered at entry: passports record birth sex, the 'X' marker is gone, visa officers are instructed to refuse on discrepancy and consider permanent fraud bars, and foreign nationals have reportedly been detained over visa issues. Documented custody harm includes a trans woman held 24 hours in a men's ward, national prison hormone-removal policies, and immigration-custody abuse. No lethal pathway is documented; violence data show no state-specific elevation; hate-crime statute and active litigation are partial but the highest court has allowed the passport rule. This sits between the criminalising 0.25 tier and the friction-heavy 0.45 tier.

entry_documents.exposure: Passports must show birth-sex marker; X discontinued; officers instructed to refuse applications on discrepancy and weigh lifetime fraud ineligibility for 'misrepresentation'; foreign citizens reportedly detained over visa issues; allied governments issue trans-specific travel advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; fraud finding requires four elements and is never automatic; policy challenged in national courts.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at entry can cascade into secondary inspection, refusal, or fraud investigation feeding the custody pathway.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Criminal bathroom offence (first offence up to one year); documented arrest under a sibling law with handcuffing and 24-hour holding in a men's ward; national corrections bureau mandates hormone removal and haircut policies; immigration-custody forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse reported.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National ruling guarantees hormone therapy for state/province prisoners (Sept 2024); suits pending.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A restroom encounter escalates from trespass demand to arrest to birth-sex ward placement.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division law criminalises restroom use per birth sex in government buildings and private businesses including hospitals; 4 state/provinces criminalise in some circumstances; 9+ restrict all government buildings; 6 extend to private settings.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 state/provinces, 4 units and the capital district have no mapped ban; trespass statute requires refusal to depart, not automatic arrest.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Visitor's route through any covered premises carries exposure; hospital restrooms implicate emergency-care settings.

care_services.exposure: 27 state/provinces ban minor care; national rules proposed to bar insurance for under-18 care; hospitals subpoenaed for under-19 patient records; crisis-line youth services shut; visitor minors may face care denial and records exposure.
care_services.protection: None documented for visiting minors; adult care access not documented as restricted for visitors.
care_services.interaction: A travelling family seeking care could trigger records disclosure or investigation.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: 'Gender ideology' framed alongside violent extremism in counterterrorism strategy; schools and teachers criminally threatened for facilitating social transition; state law defines sex binary-only (bill pending); 2026 state law mandates disclosure of trans minors to parents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Counterterrorism text disclaims targeting mere disagreement; employment-discrimination ruling and hate-crime statute remain in force.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing licenses enforcement against visible trans presence and against families.

minors_guardians.exposure: Mandatory 3-day parental disclosure; care bans across 27 state/provinces; proposed felony liability (2022, blocked) for parents seeking out-of-state care; teacher-prosecution order; school pronoun bans; sports exclusions since 2020.
minors_guardians.protection: 2019 board retained parental-consent routes; felony bill blocked in upper chamber; litigation pending on key measures.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian's travel with a trans minor risks disclosure, care denial and state inquiry during the visit.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state/province-specific violence data above the general homicide rate identified; national hate-incident statistics cover sexual orientation broadly; police enforcement documented against facilities use rather than street assault.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; courts actively review and sometimes enjoin measures.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Not documented whether police respond adequately to anti-trans violence against visitors.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Whether the misdemeanour/felony classification stands and whether the 16 June 2026 narrowing remains in force are unresolved; enforcement against visitors not yet recorded; pending binary-only bill could broaden definitions.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active civil-rights suit on due-process, equal-protection and privacy grounds filed before the effect date; legal-aid FAQ for document rules; several national orders enjoined.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Litigation outcomes could narrow or leave the criminal ban operative during any visit.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.25-C pairs birth-sex prison housing with a cross-dressing arrest statute but brief sentences and no universal exposure. Here the exposure is universal (every restroom, including private businesses) with up to one year jail, plus national entry-document engineering — materially worse than 0.25-C despite similar sentence ceilings.

0.45-D's registration/database regime creates durable exposure with harassment and eviction as typical harms and imprisonment uncommon. This jurisdiction shares the universal-discovery architecture but adds an explicit criminal statute with jail time and documented misgendered custody, sitting below 0.45-D.

0.15-B features repeated border detention, abusive cells, withheld care and delayed habeas — routine severe custody after discovery. Here detention is possible but not the routine outcome, courts and litigation function, and no lethal pathway is documented, so this is clearly less dangerous than 0.15-B, though the gap is narrower for outed travellers in the division.

0.75-C has trained officers, tribunal review, brief detention and no criminal exposure. Reaching that level would require the criminal bathroom law enjoined, the passport rule reversed, and custody-placement harm remedied — none documented here.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime chains discovery to consequence: the national document rule makes the passport itself an outing instrument, the visa cable converts discrepancy into refusal or a potential lifetime fraud bar, and within the division the unavoidable act of using a restroom is a misdemeanour reaching hospitals, restaurants and gas stations, with documented arrest practice elsewhere showing handcuffing and men's-ward holding. Custody placement by birth sex is corroborated at national level by hormone-removal prison policies and immigration-custody abuse. For a family, minor-specific laws (care bans, records subpoenas, mandatory parental disclosure, teacher-prosecution directives) convert any care-seeking or schooling interaction into investigation exposure. Mitigation is partial and contested: litigation is active, several orders enjoined, the hate-crime statute operates, and most mapped state/provinces lack bathroom bans — but the traveller's exposure is governed by the harshest operative rule in the jurisdiction visited, which here criminalises a universal act. No execution pathway or organised lethal targeting is documented, keeping this above the 0.15 tier; the criminal universal exposure and compounding entry rules keep it in the High Risk band.
